title: Semi-free replacement of a dg module
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], enlarged to contain the module categories below. A small dg category $\mathcal B$ over $\mathbf Z$ has a set of objects and cochain complexes $\mathcal B(U,V)$, with unital associative chain-map compositions. A cochain complex has differential of degree $1$ with square zero. A right dg module $M$ has complexes $M(U)$ and unital associative chain-map actions $M(V)\otimes\mathcal B(U,V)\to M(U)$. Its cohomology is $H^r(M(U))=\ker d^r/\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}$; acyclic means these groups vanish for every $U,r$, and an objectwise quasi-isomorphism induces isomorphisms on all these groups. The representable module $\mathcal B(-,U)$ has action given by composition. The shift $M[n]$ has $M[n]^r=M^{r+n}$, differential $(-1)^n d_M$, and the unchanged right graded action. A graded module map of degree $r$ satisfies $f(ma)=f(m)a$; the complex of such maps is $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(M,N)$, with differential $df=d_Nf-(-1)^rfd_M$. A module $P$ is homotopically projective if this complex is acyclic for every objectwise acyclic $N$. A semi-free module $P$ has a filtration by dg submodules $0=P_0\subset P_1\subset\cdots$, with $P=\bigcup_{i\geq0}P_i$, each inclusion split as a graded module map, and each quotient $P_{i+1}/P_i$ isomorphic as a dg module to a coproduct of shifts of representables.

Every right dg $\mathcal B$-module $M$ admits an objectwise quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to M$ from a semi-free module $P$.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, section 14.8 (right modules by passage to the opposite dg category), printed pp. 36-37; compare the dg-algebra case in Stacks tag 09KP, label dga-lemma-resolve, literature/stacks-project/dga.tex. Section 14.8 explicitly states the dg-category version.

proof.text: For an object $U$ and integer $s$, write $h_U[-s]=\mathcal B(-,U)[-s]$ with generator $e=1_U$ in degree $s$. The unit is closed: the chain-map composition identity gives $d(1_U)=d(1_U)1_U+1_Ud(1_U)=2d(1_U)$, hence $d(1_U)=0$. At an object $V$, elements are finite sums $ea$ with $a\in\mathcal B(V,U)$ and $|ea|=s+|a|$. Its differential is $d(ea)=(-1)^s e\,d_{\mathcal B}a$. A prescribed homogeneous value $e\mapsto z\in N(U)^s$ extends uniquely to a graded right-module map by $ea\mapsto za$; when $dz=0$, this is a dg-module map since $d_N(za)=(-1)^s z\,d_{\mathcal B}a$. This is a direct computation with the representable, shift, and module definitions in the statement.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, §13.3 (printed p. 33) and §14.8 (printed p. 36); explicit generator expansion of successive attachments for right modules.

proof.text: Set $P_0=0$. Let $I_1$ be the set of triples $(U,s,z)$ where $U$ is an object of $\mathcal B$, $s\in\mathbf Z$, and $z\in M(U)^s$ satisfies $dz=0$. These are sets in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Form the objectwise direct sum $P_1=\bigoplus_{(U,s,z)\in I_1}h_U[-s]$. Its generator $e_{U,s,z}$ has degree $s$ and differential zero. Step 1 defines a dg-module map $q_1:P_1\to M$ by $q_1(e_{U,s,z}a)=za$. In particular every cocycle of $M(U)$ has a specified cocycle lift in $P_1(U)$.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, §13.3 (printed p. 33) and §14.8 (printed p. 36); explicit generator expansion of successive attachments for right modules.

proof.text:
Inductively, suppose that $P_i$ and a dg-module map $q_i:P_i\to M$ have been constructed, for $i\geq1$. Take the set $J_i$ of all tuples $(U,r,x,y)$ with $x\in P_i(U)^r$, $dx=0$, $y\in M(U)^{r-1}$ and $q_i(x)=d_My$. Form the graded right module
$$P_{i+1}^{\#}=P_i^{\#}\oplus\bigoplus_{(U,r,x,y)\in J_i}h_U[1-r]^{\#}.$$
For the new generator $t=t_{U,r,x,y}$ of degree $r-1$, prescribe
$$d(t a)=x a+(-1)^{r-1}t\,d_{\mathcal B}a,$$
and retain the old differential on $P_i$. The superscript $\#$ means that the differential has been forgotten. For each new summand at an object $V$, the coefficient maps $a\mapsto xa$ into $P_i(V)$ and $a\mapsto d_{\mathcal B}a$ into the same shifted representable are additive maps on $\mathcal B(V,U)$ itself. Thus the formula respects all additive relations in that complex, even if it has torsion; no basis over $\mathbf Z$ is chosen. All direct sums consist of finite-support sums, so these operators combine to an additive degree-one operator at each object.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, §13.3 (printed p. 33) and §14.8 (printed p. 36); explicit generator expansion of successive attachments for right modules.

proof.text:
The operator in Step 3 squares to zero: on a new generator multiple $ta$ its square is
$$d^2(ta)=(-1)^r x\,d_{\mathcal B}a+(-1)^{r-1}x\,d_{\mathcal B}a=0,$$
using $dx=0$ and $d_{\mathcal B}^2=0$; it squares to zero on the old summand by induction.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, §13.3 (printed p. 33) and §14.8 (printed p. 36); explicit generator expansion of successive attachments for right modules.

proof.text: For homogeneous composable $a,b$, expand $d_{\mathcal B}(ab)=(d_{\mathcal B}a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d_{\mathcal B}b$ in the formula for $d(tab)$. The result is $d(ta)b+(-1)^{r-1+|a|}(ta)d_{\mathcal B}b$, which is exactly the dg-module action identity. The old summand already satisfies this identity. Thus $P_{i+1}$ is a right dg module. Units and associativity of the graded action are inherited summand by summand from $P_i$ and the representables.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, §13.3 (printed p. 33) and §14.8 (printed p. 36); explicit generator expansion of successive attachments for right modules.

proof.text:
Define $q_{i+1}$ on the old summand to be $q_i$ and on a new generator multiple by $q_{i+1}(ta)=ya$. These formulas give a graded module map by the generator-to-value calculation in Step 1, which does not require the value $y$ to be closed. Then
$$q_{i+1}d(ta)=q_i(x)a+(-1)^{r-1}y\,d_{\mathcal B}a=d_M(ya),$$
since $q_i(x)=d_My$. Hence $q_{i+1}$ is a dg-module map extending $q_i$.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, §13.3 (printed p. 33) and §14.8 (printed p. 36); explicit generator expansion of successive attachments for right modules.

proof.text:
The inclusion $P_i\hookrightarrow P_{i+1}$ is a dg-module inclusion and splits as a graded module map by projection onto the first summand of Step 3. Modulo $P_i$, the term $xa$ in the new differential vanishes. Therefore the quotient differential is $d(ta)=(-1)^{r-1}t\,d_{\mathcal B}a$, the differential of $h_U[1-r]$. Consequently
$$P_{i+1}/P_i\cong\bigoplus_{(U,r,x,y)\in J_i}h_U[1-r]$$
as dg modules. In addition, every cycle $x\in P_i(U)^r$ whose image under $q_i$ is the boundary $d_My$ becomes the boundary $d(t_{U,r,x,y}1_U)=x1_U+(-1)^{r-1}t_{U,r,x,y}d(1_U)=x$ in $P_{i+1}(U)$, using the closed unit from Step 1.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, §13.3 (printed p. 33) and §14.8 (printed p. 36); explicit generator expansion of successive attachments for right modules.

proof.text: Repeat Steps 3–7 by induction on $i\geq1$. Take the increasing union $P(V)=\bigcup_iP_i(V)$ at each object $V$, with differential and actions inherited from the stages. They are well-defined because every inclusion is a dg-module map; their identities hold at the stage containing the elements in question. The compatible maps $q_i$ define a dg-module map $q:P\to M$. The filtration starting with $P_0=0$ is exhaustive by this definition of $P$. Its first quotient is the direct sum in Step 2, and all later quotients and graded splittings are given in Step 7. Thus $P$ is semi-free exactly as defined in the statement.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, §13.3 (printed p. 33) and §14.8 (printed p. 36); explicit generator expansion of successive attachments for right modules.

proof.text: Fix an object $U$ and an integer $r$. Each class in $H^r(M(U))$ has a cocycle representative $z\in M(U)^r$. The generator $e_{U,r,z}\in P_1(U)^r\subseteq P(U)^r$ is closed and maps to $z$ by Step 2, so $H^r(q(U))$ is surjective.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, §13.3 (printed p. 33) and §14.8 (printed p. 36); explicit generator expansion of successive attachments for right modules.

proof.text: For injectivity, let a closed $x\in P(U)^r$ map to a boundary $d_My$. Since $P$ is an increasing union, $x$ belongs to some $P_i(U)$ with $i\geq1$. The inclusion $P_i(U)\to P(U)$ is injective, so $dx=0$ already in $P_i(U)$. The tuple $(U,r,x,y)$ belongs to $J_i$, and Step 7 supplies $t_{U,r,x,y}\in P_{i+1}(U)^{r-1}$ with $dt=x$. Thus the class of $x$ is zero. This proves injectivity, and hence $H^r(q(U))$ is an isomorphism for every $U,r$. The map $q$ is therefore the required objectwise quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, §13.3 (printed p. 33) and §14.8 (printed p. 36); explicit generator expansion of successive attachments for right modules.

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph 2: explicit generator construction following the successive-cell method of Drinfeld §§13.3 and 14.8, with all differential, quotient, and cohomology calculations written out.

split_report.summary: Expanded the right dg-module semi-free resolution explicitly. The first stage has a generator for every target cocycle. At each successor stage a generator of degree r−1 is attached for every cycle x of degree r with image dy, with dt=x and q(t)=y. The proof checks the differential square, action Leibniz identity, chain-map identity, graded splittings and shifted-representable quotients, then proves cohomology surjectivity and injectivity directly in the union. Three initially proposed auxiliary nodes were folded into the proof because their construction/calculation arguments are elementary. No new nodes and no Mathlib leaves.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint proof paragraph 2: projective dg-module models used for the finite derived mapping-complex adjunction before total inverse limit.
